entries.value: TB-500 is not approved by the FDA or any other major regulatory body for human use. It is classified as a research peptide and sold under research-use-only designations.

TB-500 and Thymosin Beta-4 are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) under the S2 category (Peptide Hormones, Growth Factors, Related Substances, and Mimetics). Several athletes have received bans for testing positive for Thymosin Beta-4.

NSW Health reported (19 Oct 2026) 1,180 presentations to NSW emergency departments associated with peptide use between 1 July 2025 and 30 September 2026. The release does not break this figure down by peptide. The release names TB-500 among the peptides that products may claim to contain and states: "None of these peptides are currently approved in Australia for any purpose."

Poisons Standard (October 2026; F2026L01327; in force from 1 October 2026): "TB-500" is a named Schedule 4 entry and is listed in Appendix D, clause 5, item 38 ("Poisons for which possession without authority is illegal"). Thymosin beta 4 has its own entry (item 39). Neither the instrument nor the NSW release defines the structure behind the name "TB-500", so this page does not state that either refers specifically to Ac-LKKTETQ, the fragment described here. Scheduling is implemented through State and Territory legislation.
